notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Round money only via round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 3x, 2 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0004] Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc: In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`).
  (learned from task E03 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0006] Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by: Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver per finance policy FIN-2026-03: accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise `BillingError("approval_required")` when the amount exceeds the threshold and no approver is given; amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0003] Reject bools when validating integer fields: When validating an int field such as quantity, check isinstance(x, bool) first because bool is a subclass of int; use `isinstance(quantity, bool) or not isinstance(quantity, int) or quantity <= 0`.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0005] Money operations take idempotency_key and check it first: Every function that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` and check it before any state validation: scan `ledgerly.audit.events()` for an entry with the same key and return the original result (the same record) without reapplying. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry written via `audit.record`.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source INC-204; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0007] Write audit amounts as float(amount): When recording amounts in `ledgerly.audit.record` entries, pass `float(amount)`; the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)

excluded.at-0002: superseded by at-0008 (the old rule was wrong)
